messages.content: Predict this child’s own response. This game is played by video call with pictures. You have chosen a cartoon to represent yourself and have been introduced to three other children of your age and gender, represented by cartoons. Your group has four members including you. In each round everyone starts with 2 new tokens and makes the same kind of choice. You may keep both tokens: you receive 2 tokens from your own allocation and the other three receive none from it. Or give your 2 tokens to the group: they turn into 4 tokens, with 1 going to each of the four group members, including you. Each other child can also keep or give; each one who gives adds 1 token to your earnings. You see your own choice but are not shown the other children’s choices during the rounds. The tokens you collect are presented as exchangeable for a video prize at the end of the game. A separate participation gift certificate is available even if you stop. You have been shown what keeping and giving do and checked your understanding before the rounds. The two pictured choices change position and color across rounds. This question expresses the allocations by their meaning. Answer only give_to_group (turn your 2 tokens into 4, one for each group member) or keep_for_self (keep your 2).

You are 7 years old; your recorded gender is female. Current game instruction: You were told to take time to think and wait until the experimenter asked to hear your choice. This is the first round; you have no earlier game choices. You are now at round 1, with 2 new tokens. You have received no information about the other children’s choices. Which allocation do you choose?
give_to_group
